chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Hamadani, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who stays still in the water. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, but he should not immerse himself in it; and the woman should not stay still in the water because she carries the water with her private part.'

key_terms.يَسْتَنْقِعُ: stays still/stands in water (up to neck)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fasting person immersing themselves in water according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between *istinqa'* (submerging the head to cool or refresh) and full immersion (*ghams*), permitting the former for fasting men while cautioning against it due to potential impurity, and prohibiting it for women specifically due to the retention of water in the private area (*farj*). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the state of ritual purity (*taharah*) during fasting, linking physical actions to the validity of worship through the lens of bodily mechanics.
